item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: One Car Photo Three Sizes

turns.text: I need this car photo in three sizes: square, 4:5 for the feed, and 9:16 for stories. Send three separate pictures. Keep the whole car in each; blurred photo padding is fine if a crop won't work. No text.

item.tests: Tests delivering three distinct aspect-ratio adaptations of one source while keeping the complete subject in every version.

answer_sheet.Sizes and deliverables: Three separate images: 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16. A 640-pixel longest edge is fine.
answer_sheet.Subject to preserve: The whole red car, including both ends, roof and wheels.
answer_sheet.Padding and composition: Use blurred source-photo padding wherever cropping would cut off the car. Otherwise composition is your call.
answer_sheet.Style and wording: Preserve the original photo, with no added text or restyling.

must_haves: Three separate images are delivered, rather than one collage.
The three frames have ratios of 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 respectively.
Every version shows the same red hatchback from the attached photo.
The complete car, including roof, wheels and both ends, is visible in every version.
The car retains its original proportions and appearance in all versions.
Any padding is a blurred version of the source photo, and no version contains added text.

turns.text: I need this car pic in three sizes: square, 4:5 for the feed, and 9:16 for stories. Send three separate pictures. Keep the whole car in each; blurred photo padding is fine if a crop won't work. No text. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has run, and no credits have been spent.**

The cheapest—and best-quality—way is **ordinary resizing with blurred photo padding**, not AI generation. That keeps the original car intact without redrawing it.

| Method | Cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Non-AI resize/padding in a free photo editor | **0 Magic Hour credits** | Best fit for your request; I don’t have a non-AI resize/export tool connected here. |
| Magic Hour AI editing, three separate 640px images | **Estimated 15 credits total** | Using free-plan Flux-2-Klein at its listed starting price of 5 credits per image. AI may alter car details. |

For a smaller set, use **640×640**, **512×640** (4:5), and **360×640** (9:16), each with the whole photo centered over a blurred copy and **no added text**.

**Cheaper/smaller:** the non-AI route avoids credits entirely. Smaller AI outputs than the available 640px setting aren’t a listed cheaper option; “shorter” only applies to video.

Would you prefer **free-editor instructions**, or proceed with the **three AI edits at an estimated 15 credits**?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—the free-editor instructions for the three sizes, with no credits spent.

turns.agent:
Use **Photopea.com** in your browser. No Magic Hour tools are needed, so **this spends 0 Magic Hour credits**.

### Make the square version
1. Choose **File → New** and set the canvas to **640 × 640 pixels**.
2. Choose **File → Open & Place** and select `car-red.jpg`.
3. Make the blurred background:
   - Enlarge the photo proportionally until it covers the entire canvas. Cropping this background layer is fine.
   - Press **Enter**, then choose **Filter → Blur → Gaussian Blur**. Try **20–30 px**.
4. Choose **File → Open & Place** again and select the same photo.
5. Resize this top copy proportionally to **640 px wide**, keeping the **entire original photo visible**. Center it horizontally and vertically.
6. Choose **File → Export As → JPG**, set quality around **90%**, and save as `car-square.jpg`.

### Make the other two versions
Repeat the same steps in two new documents:

| File name | Canvas size | Top photo |
|---|---|---|
| `car-feed-4x5.jpg` | **512 × 640 px** | Fit to 512 px wide; center |
| `car-stories-9x16.jpg` | **360 × 640 px** | Fit to 360 px wide; center |

**Important:** Keep the photo’s proportions locked when resizing. Only the blurred background should be cropped—not the sharp top photo. Don’t add any text layers.

You’ll have **three separate pictures**, each showing the whole car.
